title: Element Appearing More Than 25% In Sorted Array
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers sorted in non-decreasing order. Exactly one value occurs **more than 25%** of the time, that is, strictly more than `n / 4` times in the array. Every other value occurs at most `n / 4` times.

Print that value.

**Follow-up:** a single scan over the array is easy. Interviewers asked for `O(log n)` time for the search itself, using the fact that the array is sorted.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: Print the value that occurs more than 25% of the time.
constraints: The array is sorted in non-decreasing order.
Exactly one value occurs strictly more than n / 4 times; every other value occurs at most n / 4 times.

examples.explanation: The value 2 appears 3 times and 3 > 8 / 4 = 2. Every other value appears once.
Here n / 4 = 1, so the answer must appear at least twice. Only 7 does.
A single element appears 100% of the time.

hints: In a sorted array equal values sit next to each other. A value that fills more than a quarter of the array covers a long contiguous block.
A block longer than n / 4 must contain at least one of the elements at the positions n/4, n/2 and 3n/4 (integer division). So only three candidate values need checking.
To count a candidate in O(log n), binary search for the first and last position where it occurs, and test whether that count is greater than n / 4.
